clinician.final_diagnosis: CM originating from primary breast carcinoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with bilateral axillary and trunk nodules, asthenia, anorexia, and 10 kg weight loss. A punch biopsy of the skin nodules revealed diffuse infiltration of atypical cells consistent with metastatic undifferentiated carcinoma (E003). Immunohistochemistry on the biopsy confirmed mammary origin, consistent with lobular-type metastatic adenocarcinoma (ER+, PR-, HER2- faint/negative) (E004). Elevated tumor markers (CA 15-3 >500 U/mL, CEA 6.37 ng/mL) further supported the diagnosis (E005). Four months after initiating treatment, a CT scan showed significant ascites and pleural effusion (E008). The patient died of her illness 7 months after the diagnosis of CM originating from primary breast carcinoma.
